Issued at 131 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Today through Friday.

As of early this morning, the front that brought rain to central 
Indiana is south of the forecast area, but as the next low pressure 
system moves in from the Central Plains later this morning, that 
front is expected to push back to the north. Ahead of the boundary, 
poleward moisture advection characterized by an 850 mb low-level jet 
of 40-50 kt will lift surface dew points into the low-to-mid 60s, 
creating a short window in the mid to late afternoon hours where 
MLCAPE could reach 750 to 1250 J/kg along and south of the I-70 
corridor by early afternoon. Kinematic fields are quite robust, with 
500 mb mid-level flow around 50-60 kt yielding effective bulk shear 
of 45-55 kt. This deep-layer shear will favor organized multi-cell 
clusters and linear segments capable of bowing along with an 
increasing threat for a few discrete supercells late this afternoon 
into the evening. 

Low-level 0-1 km storm-relative helicity values of 100-150 m2/s2 
will support an isolated brief spin-up along the warm front, but 
that threat will be conditional on the front location and extent of 
daytime warming. Thus the dominant convective hazard will be 
damaging straight-line downdraft winds up to 60 mph via momentum 
transport with the tornado threat being secondary. HREF ensemble 
members (HRRR, FV3, and ARW) depict initial convective development 
across west-central Indiana between 18Z and 20Z, progressing 
across the Indianapolis metro area between 21Z and 00Z, and 
exiting eastern counties by 02Z-04Z with the potential that this
occurs over 2 rounds through the day QPF will average between 
0.50 and 1.00 inches; localized training could produce minor 
nuisance ponding in poor drainage areas, but the progressive 
motion of the system will mitigate widespread flash flood 
concerns.

The cold front will push southeast of the forecast area by 03Z, 
bringing an end to heavier precipitation with lingering light rain 
through the night. Cold air advection will ensue overnight as 850 mb 
temperatures plummet from +12C to near +1C by Friday afternoon. The 
tight pressure gradient between the departing surface low over 
eastern Canada and a Canadian high building into the Plains will 
generate efficient boundary-layer momentum transfer. Diurnal mixing 
into the 850-800 mb layer will tap into 35-40 kt ambient flow, 
supporting sustained northwest winds of 18-25 mph with frequent 
gusts of 25-35 mph Friday afternoon. Cyclonic flow and steep low-
level lapse rates will foster an extensive stratocumulus deck, 
particularly across the northern two-thirds of the CWA. Highs on 
Friday will remain suppressed, ranging from the upper 50s north to
the lower 60s south. Winds Friday night should keep frost 
formation limited even as temperatures drop into the mid to upper 
30s, but sheltered areas could see some frost ahead of a 
widespread frost Saturday night.

Saturday Through Wednesday.

A broad longwave trough will anchor across the eastern CONUS on 
Saturday as a strong  surface anticyclone shifts from the Upper 
Mississippi Valley southeastward across the Ohio Valley through 
Sunday. The core of the cold pool will sit overhead Saturday, 
keeping 850 mb temperatures around 0C to +2C. Despite clearing skies 
and subsidence, daytime highs on Saturday will struggle to reach out 
of the mid 50s, 10-15 degrees below normal.

Saturday night into Sunday morning represents the primary frost and 
low-end freeze window of the period. The surface high center will 
settle directly over central Indiana by 09Z Sunday, decoupling the 
boundary layer and yielding calm winds, clear skies, and a very dry 
ambient air mass with dew points in the upper 20s to low 30s. Strong 
radiational cooling will cause overnight minimum temperatures to 
drop into the lower to mid-30s across the entire forecast area, with 
rural drainage basins and traditional cold spots likely dropping near 
freezing. Widespread frost is expected across central Indiana, and 
freeze conditions are probable in sheltered rural areas. Frost and 
freeze headlines will likely be required as confidence remains high 
across deterministic GFS, ECMWF, and their respective ensemble 
suites.

The anticyclone will drift eastward toward the Mid-Atlantic on 
Sunday, allowing insolation to rebound highs into the upper 50s and 
lower 60s. Lows Sunday night will remain cool, in the upper 30s to 
lower 40s, with patchy frost confined to far eastern rural valleys 
before low-level winds back to the south.

For Monday through Wednesday, the synoptic pattern transitions as 
upper-level ridging builds over the eastern states and a deep trough 
carves out over the western CONUS. Steady south-southwesterly return 
flow will drive a significant warm air advection regime across the 
Ohio Valley. 850 mb temperatures will moderate to +10C to +13C, 
pushing daytime highs into the lower 70s on Monday and mid-70s on
